To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) joint subchannel allocation outperforms disjoint subchannel allocation for both open and closed access femtocell networks; (ii) for dense femtocell network, closed access femtocel networks outperform open access femtocell network in terms of system throughput; (iii) for sparse femtocell network and closed access femtcells, the system throughput can be increased by allowing femtocells to share the same subchannels with macrocells;

the joint subchannel allocation outperforms the disjoint subchannel allocation when the femtocells are in open access and the femtocell densities are sparse, while the disjoint subchannel scheme performs better than the joint scheme when the femtocell are in closed access and the femtotcell densities are dense.
the optimized joint and open access subchannel allocations provide high network throughput in sparse and dense two-tier femtocell networks.
